sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Freeborn County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
The Freeborn County Government Center at 411 Broadway South in Albert Lea houses both offices, with mail going to PO Box 1147, Albert Lea, MN 56007. The Assessor values and classifies property, and the Auditor-Treasurer computes and collects the tax.

  • Assessor: 507-377-5176. Open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Auditor-Treasurer: 507-377-5117 for taxes and the real estate drop box.

Freeborn County describes its setup as a true county assessor system, so the county assesses every parcel, including those in small cities and townships. The auditor's office keeps records, transfer cards, tax maps and certificates of value on about 22,000 parcels and records changes such as transfers, sales, splits and mortgages. It also collects special assessments for cities and townships and passes them on.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Freeborn County?
sections.html:
Freeborn County is on Minnesota's southern border with Iowa. Albert Lea is both the seat and the largest city, and the county forms the Albert Lea micropolitan area. It was created February 20, 1855 from parts of Blue Earth and Rice counties and is named for William Freeborn, a pioneer, merchant and territorial legislator.

The Shell Rock River flows south out of Albert Lea Lake toward Iowa, and Myre-Big Island State Park is inside the county. The land totals 722 square miles, 707 of them dry. The 2020 census counted 30,895 residents, and the Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 30,440, a drop of 1.5 percent.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows a median owner-occupied value of $171,100, an owner-occupied rate of 79.5 percent and median household income of $71,023. Median gross rent is $849. The county issued only 13 building permits in 2025, and the average commute is 19.7 minutes.

Three in five residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census, 58.2 percent, with 7.4 percent of the 14,114 housing units vacant. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,316, and owners without one report $563. About one in four residents, 25.4 percent, is 65 or older, and 90.0 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. Estate sales and long-held homes are therefore a regular part of the Albert Lea market.

sections.h2: What are the Freeborn County payment dates?
sections.html:
The two real estate installments fall in May and October. Minnesota's statute requires payment before May 16 and before October 16, and agricultural property gets until November 15 for the second half. The same law adds a penalty of 2 percent for homestead or 4 percent for non-homestead when a due date slips (Minn. Stat. 279.01), and then an extra 1 percent each month through December.

Online payments can be completed before midnight on the due date, and they are credited to that day's business. The county notes that it may take up to four working days for the credit to appear on its Beacon tax site, so keep the confirmation.

sections.h2: What is the Freeborn County reassessment, and does it affect my sale?
sections.html:
Yes, it can. The Assessor's Office announced that appraisers began visiting properties in June 2026 to photograph them and verify characteristics for the 2027 assessment, which sets property taxes payable in 2028. Minnesota requires a physical inspection at least once every five years.

The review covers Albert Lea residential property, the small cities of Clarks Grove, Glenville, Manchester and Myrtle, and the townships of Hayward, Manchester, Moscow, Oakland and Pickerel Lake. Appraisers drive county vehicles, wear safety vests and carry badges, and postcards are mailed to owners before the visit. They may ask to see the inside of the house.

You may decline, but the cost is real. A property owner can refuse in person or in writing, and the assessor then estimates the interior condition by assumption. Under Minn. Stat. 274.13 as the county quotes it, a board may not grant a value or class change that benefits a property whose owner refused inspection. Refusing does not stop you from attending the board of appeal and equalization.

sections.h2: How does Freeborn County set values?
sections.html:
The assessor estimates what a property would likely sell for on the open market. State standards then require values between 90 and 105 percent of market value, measured from a sample of sales rather than any single sale. The county analyzes sales to build a formula, applies it to all properties, and tests the result against statistical requirements.

The Assessor posts sales reports for the period November 1, 2025 to November 1, 2026. They cover Albert Lea residential sales, small city residential, township residential, duplexes and triplexes, rural residential land, vacant land and agricultural sales. Reading the report for your category is a quick way to see whether your value is in line before you list.

  • Real estate market trends, interest rates, local economic conditions and supply all feed into value.
  • A higher tax bill does not always mean a higher value. Local government spending, school bonds, legislative changes and new construction in the county also move the bill.

sections.h2: What if I owe back tax on a Freeborn County property?
sections.html:
Use the county's delinquent tax list, and pay attention to its "Interest Figured To" date. Interest rises on the first of each month, so the figure shown goes out of date, and the county posts an updated list in the first week of each month. Call the auditor at 507-377-5117 for an exact payoff.

If a parcel has several years of delinquency and you cannot pay all of it, the county's rule is that you pay the most recent year first. Delinquent real property taxes are applied in inverse order, starting with the latest year. Plan to clear the full balance before closing, because the county auditor checks for delinquent tax before it enters a transfer on the books (Minn. Stat. 272.12).

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Freeborn County valuation?
sections.html:
Start by calling the assessor at 507-377-5176 when your notice arrives. If a conversation does not help, the local board of appeal and equalization hears the first formal appeal in April or May (Minn. Stat. 274.01), then the county board in June, and finally the Minnesota Tax Court with a petition due April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Bring comparable sales and photographs, not a general complaint about the bill. The county's FAQ adds that a bill can rise for reasons other than your value, including local spending and school bonds, and none of those is something a valuation appeal can reverse.

faqs.q: What is the Freeborn County Assessor's phone number?
faqs.a: It is 507-377-5176, at 411 Broadway South in Albert Lea. The Assessor's Office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Freeborn County tax by card?
faqs.a: The county charges $2.00 for card payments from $0 to $60 and 2.35 percent for payments of $61 or more. An e-check carries a flat $2.00 fee.

faqs.q: Is there a drop box for Freeborn County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Real Estate Taxes Drop Off box sits inside the Law Enforcement entrance of the Freeborn County Government Center. Call 507-377-5117 if you need help.

faqs.q: Which Freeborn County areas are being reassessed for 2027?
faqs.a: Albert Lea residential property, the small cities of Clarks Grove, Glenville, Manchester and Myrtle, and the townships of Hayward, Manchester, Moscow, Oakland and Pickerel Lake.

faqs.q: Which delinquent year do I pay first in Freeborn County?
faqs.a: The most recent delinquent year. The county says delinquent real property tax is paid in inverse order, so a partial payment goes against the latest year first.
